summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and diffuse body pain, including right hip pain, after a prolonged decline in well-being. She has a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, type 1 diabetes with complications, gastroparesis, fibromyalgia, and chronic pain. Admission evaluation revealed hyponatremia, fluid overload, and drug-induced constipation likely exacerbated by opioid use. There was no evidence of infection on blood or dialysis fluid cultures, and imaging showed no acute abnormalities. An irrigation of the peritoneal cavity was performed to improve dialysis efficacy. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, medication adjustments, and reduced opioid use. She was discharged home with optimized pain management, continued peritoneal dialysis, and follow-up plans with her specialists.
